title: Redwood Migration Demo - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Nimbus Health through parity mapping for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API. Covered endpoints mapping (chat/completions/embeddings), function calling/parsing, streaming, rate limits, batching, cost/latency tradeoffs, and Redwood Console/Optimize suggestions for cost reduction. Security questions around VPC, KMS, SOC2 were raised. Agreed next steps: send mapping doc & sample SDK snippets, security whitepaper, pricing sheet, and schedule proof-of-concept bench next week.
topics: function calling differences and schema mapping
security: VPC/private deployment, KMS, audit logs, SOC2
next_steps: Send parity mapping doc and example SDK snippets (Lena)
Provision pilot account and test dataset for POC (Nimbus)
Schedule 1-hour POC benchmark next week (mutually agreed)
action_items: Lena: email parity mapping + pricing by 2025-12-03
Marcus: attach SOC2 + security whitepaper by 2025-12-03
Nimbus/Sara: share sample prompt set and PI-free dataset by 2025-12-05
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-01 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Nimbus CTO), Jon Ruiz (Nimbus Lead ML Eng), Priya Menon (Nimbus Security)

Summary: quick migration walkthrough for parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Showed code snippets, Console UI, and Optimize recommendations. Security Qs on VPC/KMS.

Topics: intro, current stack (OpenAI + Together embeddings), mapping chat/completions -> Redwood chat/generate, function calling, streaming behavior, embedding dims & similarity, cost/latency tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted, next steps.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate; auto-transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll get started. I see Sara Jon and Priya on the call, thanks for making time. Marcus and I will run through a migration demo mapping from the OpenAI/Anthropic/Together setups you described in the discovery thread, and then walk the Console and Optimize bits.
[00:18] Sara Patel: yep thanks, we got about 45 minutes, hope that's enough, we mainly want to confirm parity and double-check cost/latency impact.
[00:25] Marcus Chen: great, yes we'll try to keep it tight. quick agenda: API parity - how calls map, function calling behavior, streaming, embeddings, then Console + Optimize suggestions, and security questions at the end.
[00:36] Jon Ruiz: also we've got a small prompt set and retrieval pipeline we can share live; want to see how batching and caching work vs OpenAI.
[00:44] Lena Park: perfect. quick background from your discovery notes: you're using OpenAI chat endpoints for assistant flows, Anthropic for safety-sensitive reranks on some flows, and Together for a custom-tuned summarization that we host. is that right?
[00:55] Jon Ruiz: mm yes, OpenAI for general chatgpt flows, Anthropic for a second-stage safety filter, and Together for a custom-tuned summarization that we host.
[01:06] Marcus Chen: ok great. first slide, high-level mapping: Redwood exposes a single API with named model catalog entries. For chat/completions, the pattern is chat/generate (we've got compatibility wrappers if you want the completions shape), streaming uses chunked deltas and supports function/tool calling via structured JSON outputs.
[01:27] Lena Park: I'll share my screen - code sample first. here's an example turning an OpenAI chat completion call into Redwood. so original was something like openai.chat.completions.create({ messages, max_tokens, temperature }) - on Redwood you call redwood.chat.generate({ model: 'redwood/gpt-... ', input: messages, max_tokens, temperature }) the shape is similar but note the input param supports arrays or full conversation objects.
[01:51] Jon Ruiz: is there a one-to-one mapping for message role names? we rely on 'system'/'user'/'assistant' heavily.
[01:58] Marcus Chen: yes we preserve role names. sometimes transcription might show variation but the SDK normalizes system, user, assistant.
[02:07] Sara Patel: what about function calling? that's where we saw some differences when we tried Anthropic-style tool-calls vs OpenAI's schema.
[02:15] Marcus Chen: good question. we support two patterns: the OpenAI function-calling style (functions list + call->arguments), and a Redwood structured-output mode which is more explicit about types and protobuf-like schemas. for migration we recommend starting with the OpenAI function calling compatibility mode - minimal code change. Then optionally move to structured-output for stronger validation and noise reduction.
[02:40] Jon Ruiz: does the structured-output handle nested objects? our tools return nested JSONs for enrichment.
[02:44] Marcus Chen: yes, but there's a little nuance: the policy about arrays vs maps is stricter; the schema has to be declared. we've seen transcription where arrays of unknown objects get coerced, so it's best to provide explicit schemas.
[02:58] == Speaker 1: um and also you said something about streaming differences? ==
[03:03] Lena Park: right - OpenAI streaming sends token deltas; Redwood streams in chunked events with metadata per chunk (token text, chunk_id, partial_token, token_index) so you can do more deterministic reassembly. we also attach a chunk checksum id for reordering-correction on flaky networks.
[03:22] Priya Menon: checksum id? can you repeat that, cause network reliability is huge for our telehealth flows.
[03:27] Marcus Chen: sure, each chunk carries a small seq id + checksum; the client SDK handles reordering and de-duping. if a chunk gets retried you won't get duplicate final outputs. this reduces hallucination artifacts in streaming.
[03:40] Sara Patel: interesting. latency-wise how does Redwood streaming compare? our key req is <300ms for short prompts.
[03:47] Marcus Chen: with hosted low-latency endpoints we've seen 50-150ms first-byte for small prompts; depends on model size and VPC overlay. Dedicated pools provide more predictable p99. In our benchmarks - using a 7B model quantized - p50 was ~40ms, p99 ~260ms under normal load.
[04:09] Jon Ruiz: ok that's promising. what about batching? Together/our infra batches a lot to hit throughput. Will that affect latency?
[04:17] Marcus Chen: Redwood batching is dynamic - continuous batching driven by latency SLOs. You can set per-route latency targets; the runtime adjusts batch windows. For interactive flows you set small latency SLO and we auto-batch aggressively without big latency penalty. Optimize suggests batch sizes per model/seq length.
[04:36] Lena Park: I'll pause and show a quick Console demo - live UI.
[04:41] == screen share noise ==
[04:44] Lena Park: here's the project Routes list - you can see per-route cost, token breakdown, and tracing. For migrations we typically create a route with a canary to map your existing OpenAI traffic into a Redwood route so you can validate parity before flip.
[04:59] Jon Ruiz: can we route only a percentage of traffic for specific tenants? we have multi-tenant patients.
[05:05] Marcus Chen: yes, route-level rules allow tenant-based routing, header-based, or query-based rules. RBAC integrates with SSO so only the teams you authorize can change those rules.
[05:16] Priya Menon: speaking of RBAC - what about audit logs and key management? we need HSM-backed keys for production.
[05:23] Marcus Chen: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integration. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys; for regulated workloads we recommend Private with your KMS and full audit logs shipped to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 and security pack after.
[05:40] Sara Patel: we'd likely want VPC yes, at least for the POC.
[05:44] Lena Park: noted. Marcus will attach the VPC runbook and steps.
[05:48] Marcus Chen: ok back to API parity. embeddings: you mentioned Together for some embeddings?
[05:54] Jon Ruiz: we use Together's embeddings for retrieval and vector search, dims are 1536. we also have an OpenAI embedding flow for similarity checks.
[06:03] Marcus Chen: Redwood supports embeddings endpoints; model catalog includes multiple embedding models and dims. When you migrate, you'll want to map the vector dims and the similarity metric - we recommend cosine, but we also support dot-product if you need it. We'll include a parity table: model_name -> dim -> expected behavior.
[06:20] Jon Ruiz: any quantization differences that mess with vector quality? Together used fp16 for embeddings.
[06:26] Marcus Chen: we expose quantization profile metadata. Some quantized models show small shifts in vector distribution; Optimize can recommend re-embedding or a small reweighting to keep similarity thresholds stable. We can run a quick benchmark on your sample set and give a recommended threshold delta.
[06:44] Sara Patel: on the topic of cost - what are typical unit economics when migrating? we saw Together charges vs OpenAI.
[06:51] Lena Park: for hosted usage it's usage-based pricing; the Optimize tool helps by recommending batching, caching and model substitutions. For example, for rerank flows we may suggest moving to a smaller reranker or using cached KV for repeated prefixes which can reduce per-call tokens by 30-60% depending on reuse. We'll show an example in Console optimize suggestions.
[07:12] Marcus Chen: here's a demo of Optimize: it looks at token distributions and suggests per-route quantization and batch windows; there's also a model suggestion card that shows latency vs cost tradeoffs. You can also pin model versions for canary rollouts to measure quality/regression.
[07:29] Jon Ruiz: can Optimize generate suggested config changes we can apply automatically?
[07:33] Marcus Chen: it can suggest; applying requires an operator sign-off. for Dedicated customers, Optimize can also auto-apply cost-savings policies within guardrails.
[07:42] == Speaker 2: I have a quick question about deployed model variants ==
[07:45] Marcus Chen: sure. you can have model variants with different quantization levels; the routing can fall back to a higher-quality variant when p99 latency increases. it's all part of the graceful degradation story.
[07:57] Sara Patel: one more security nit: data retention on hosted API - how long are logs or prompts stored? we need 30 day retention and an option to purge.
[08:06] Marcus Chen: hosted logs default to 90 days, but we can set shorter retention on an account level and provide purge APIs. for PII-sensitive data we usually recommend using Private or Dedicated with customer-managed retention.
[08:19] Priya Menon: do you support token redaction or deterministic hashing in transit?
[08:23] Marcus Chen: we support deterministic redaction hooks at the ingestion layer for certain patterns; it's configurable and we can demonstrate in the POC.
[08:32] Lena Park: ok switching to a quick code walkthrough for the migration. here's an example mapping OpenAI function calling to Redwood's compatibility shim - minimal changes: function list passes through, call_name -> tool invocation mapping, you may only need to adjust the schema names and SDK method.
[08:52] Jon Ruiz: can you show a quick example of re-using existing telemetry? we push traces to Datadog.
[08:58] Marcus Chen: yes we emit OpenTelemetry spans and logs; Console provides the UI, but you can forward traces to Datadog or Honeycomb. the SDKs also have built-in hooks for client-side timestamps so you can correlate.
[09:13] Sara Patel: great. how do you handle model version pinning - we need to freeze models for cert/regulatory reasons.
[09:19] Marcus Chen: you can pin an exact model digest (like version hash) and tie it to a rollout. we persist the digest in the Route config so future changes don't affect that route unless you explicitly upgrade.
[09:31] Jon Ruiz: is there a migration path we should be careful with - like tokenization differences between models? we saw small paraphrase drift when switching tokenizers that affected truncation.
[09:40] Marcus Chen: yes tokenization differences matter. we produce tokenization metadata and a tokenizer-compat check. Optimize runs a tokenization analysis on your prompt set and will flag truncation risks and recommend model padding. we'll run that for your dataset in the POC.
[09:58] Sara Patel: walk us through a concrete POC plan - what's included and what we need to provide?
[10:05] Lena Park: plan (roughly): 1) Redwood provisions a pilot project and credentials; 2) Nimbus provides a sample prompt set and a 1k-sample retrieval corpus (PI-free) + a set of canary tenants; 3) Redwood runs a migration bench (functional parity, latency/cost comparisons, embedding reprojection) and a short smoke test on streaming & function call parity; 4) interim findings and recommended config; 5) optionally a 2-week pilot with production routing on a small % of traffic.
[10:36] Jon Ruiz: that sounds good. timeline? we hope to decide before end of quarter.
[10:41] Lena Park: we can turn around the initial bench in 5 business days once we have data. Pricing options will be included.
[10:47] Priya Menon: liability and contracts - we have to get a DPA and terms redlines ready.
[10:52] Lena Park: our legal team has a standard DPA; Marcus will attach it.
[10:56] Marcus Chen: quick note on model safety: for the Anthropic rerank use-case - Redwood can route to third-party models and also provide a policy layer for lower-level safety checks. we also support policy hooks that call an internal filter before the response is returned.
[11:15] Sara Patel: any gotchas migrating Anthropic safety checks? the way their model returns conservative responses is slightly different.
[11:21] Marcus Chen: yes behavior differences exist. For safety-focused rerank we recommend running side-by-side comparisons and keeping the Anthropic call as a canary for N days. Optimize's quality monitoring can raise regression alerts if the safety score drops.
[11:36] Jon Ruiz: ok can we talk briefly about networking - you mentioned Private option - what's the deployment shape?
[11:41] Marcus Chen: Private can be VPC peered or single-tenant on-prem. For VPC we place inference workers in your subnet and control plane runs in a managed plane with mutual TLS. We can also do air-gapped on-prem bundles if needed for high compliance.
[11:58] Priya Menon: how about data egress, do logs ever leave our VPC?
[12:04] Marcus Chen: control-plane metrics can be configured to export, but for Private we can keep logs within your environment; we also provide an option to forward only anonymized aggregates.
[12:16] Lena Park: okay we're at about 12 minutes in - seems like we're making good progress, want to jump into a short live migration snippet where we run a sample prompt through both OpenAI and Redwood to compare outputs?
[12:28] Jon Ruiz: yes let's do that, we have a short prompt.
[12:31] == Live demo: running prompt through both endpoints ==
[12:34] Marcus Chen: posting the sample prompt: 'Summarize the following patient visit notes in 3 bullets, omit PII' - running on OpenAI... [12:47] OpenAI response returns: bullet list with minor PII redaction errors.
[12:51] Marcus Chen: now running Redwood route with structured-output + redaction hook... [13:02] Redwood response: cleaner bullets, redaction hook removed identifiers, schema validated.
[13:10] Jon Ruiz: looks promising; what's the delta on token usage?
[13:14] Marcus Chen: on that particular sample OpenAI used 182 input tokens + 64 output tokens, Redwood used 170 input + 58 output due to better prepended system prompt compression and prompt tokenization differences.
[13:28] Sara Patel: small wins add up. can you capture token accounting in the bench?
[13:32] Marcus Chen: yes we will produce a per-prompt token breakdown and a per-route cost estimate.
[13:36] Lena Park: quick note: sometimes transcripts or auto-generated sections flip product names, so if you see 'Redwood dedi-cated' in notes that's just transcription.
[13:47] Jon Ruiz: hah noted.
[13:50] Marcus Chen: onward - embedding migration test plan: we'll re-embed a 500-sample corpus with the recommended Redwood embedding model, compute cosine similarity vs Together's vectors, measure AUC on our relevance labels and recommend threshold shifts.
[14:08] Jon Ruiz: acceptable. also we need integration with our vector DB - we use Milvus. any extra steps?
[14:15] Marcus Chen: we output vectors as standard floats; we have Milvus connector templates. you'll need to re-index but Optimize can provide incremental reindex suggestions to minimize downtime.
[14:28] Sara Patel: security final Qs: does Redwood support SAML SSO for the Console?
[14:33] Marcus Chen: yes SAML/SSO is supported, with SCIM for user provisioning if you want.
[14:38] Priya Menon: and are there penetration test reports available?
[14:41] Marcus Chen: yes, we'll include penetration test summaries with the security pack. full reports require an NDA but summary docs are in the pack.
[14:52] Lena Park: ok we're approaching the last 20 minutes - any final deep-dive item anyone wants to prioritize?
[14:58] Jon Ruiz: can we do a quick demo of the Optimize model suggestion card for rerank flows? that's a major cost lever for us.
[15:04] Marcus Chen: sure, back to the Console - here's the rerank route, Optimize suggests a smaller reranker model for cold traffic and a cached top-k for frequent queries. it estimates a 45% token reduction for your traffic mix.
[15:19] Jon Ruiz: what's the risk of a quality regression? how is that measured?
[15:23] Marcus Chen: we run A/B tests with held-out prompt sets and compute a quality delta metric (you can plug in your custom eval function). if quality drops beyond your tolerance Optimize will revert or flag for manual review.
[15:38] Sara Patel: can we export those eval results to our analytics?
[15:41] Marcus Chen: yes, evals export to CSV and you can hook a webhook for push results.
[15:46] Lena Park: near wrap-up, I'll restate next steps: Lena sends parity mapping doc + example SDK snippets and pricing; Marcus sends security/compliance pack (SOC2, PT summary), VPC runbook, and a pilot provisioning template; Nimbus to send sample prompt set and confirm pilot tenants. schedule POC bench next week.
[16:08] Jon Ruiz: sounds good, timeline: we'll try to get the prompt set by Friday.
[16:12] Priya Menon: we'll also review DPA internally and note any must-haves.
[16:17] Lena Park: awesome. any final questions?
[16:20] Sara Patel: none from me. thanks for the thorough walkthrough.
[16:23] Marcus Chen: thanks - we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[16:27] == End transcript ==

Notes: small transcription noise (speaker mislabels and minor typos). References to docs: parity-mapping.xlsx (link in follow-up), security-pack-v2.pdf (will be attached), pricing-tier-sheet.csv (will be attached).
